Nora (Finance): Quick one for month-close: Reseller CloudForge paid Redwood a single annual invoice for a bundle that covers multiple end-customers (RF-ANNUAL-2026). They requested we split revenue to match end-customer consumption for 03/31 reporting. How do we want to handle deferrals/allocations?

Ethan (Billing): Billing sent the annual cash receipt on 2026-03-02 and issued invoice RF-ANNUAL-2026. By default we book the cash to Deferred Revenue and recognize over the contract term. We don't currently allocate to end-customers in AR.

Sofia (Revenue Ops): Two considerations: 1) Are we principal or agent here? If CloudForge is reselling and we bill them, we typically recognise gross revenue to Redwood and treat CloudForge as customer, unless contract says we act as agent. 2) For internal management reports and for some reseller SLAs we can create an allocation file that maps portions of deferred revenue to underlying customer IDs for apportioned recognition.

Liam (Accounting): From an audit perspective: recognition policy depends on contract economics. If Redwood controls the model/service and pricing, we are principal and recognise gross. If CloudForge is the primary obligor and we merely pass-through, we might recognise net. For month-end JEs, simplest is: record full prepaid into Unearned Revenue (2205) on receipt, then recognise earned portion for March based on days used. If Finance wants an allocation schedule to split recognized revenue across end-customers for internal reporting, RevOps can emit that schedule but JEs stay at reseller level.

Nora (Finance): Understood. We need both: 1) GAAP-compliant JEs for external close; 2) an internal allocation CSV to show revenue by end-customer for product analytics and chargebacks. Can Billing produce a mapping of the annual amount to end-customer usage through 03/31?

Ethan (Billing): Can do. Will output CSV with columns: reseller_inv, receipt_date, total_prepaid, end_customer_id, end_customer_usage_units, allocated_amount (pro rata by usage), days_covered, contract_term_days. ETA: upload to #finance-uploads in 90 minutes.

Sofia (Revenue Ops): We'll generate an allocation schedule that uses consumption through 03/31 to apportion the March recognition. Note this is internal only; JEs will be per reseller. We'll mark the allocation file as "internal-only" in the scheduler.

Liam (Accounting): Sample JE for external close (simplified):
```
Dr Cash/AR (1010)        $120,000   (receipt from reseller)
Cr Unearned Revenue (2205) $120,000  (defer full annual amount)
```
Then for March recognition (assuming 1/12 period earned = $10,000):
```
Dr Unearned Revenue (2205) $10,000
Cr Revenue - Dedicated (4002) $10,000
```
Nora (Finance): Perfect. For the close pack auditors want a one-paragraph memo explaining principal vs agent assessment and a copy of the allocation CSV even if it's internal. Liam, do we need to change GL treatment if the reseller agreement shows we are agent?

Liam (Accounting): Yes  if contractually agent (we only provide services and CloudForge sets price), then the revenue recognised would be net of CloudForge's margin. That requires a different JE (recognise net revenue and record payable to reseller). We need the reseller contract excerpt to confirm. Please attach the reseller agreement clause to the memo.

VendorBot: Uploaded: RF-ANNUAL-2026 contract excerpt (reseller_clause_page3) in #finance-uploads.

Ethan (Billing): CSV uploaded to #finance-uploads: 1776000000-reseller-allocation.csv. Fields included.

Sofia (Revenue Ops): Allocation file marked internal-only and attached to the close pack folder. We'll include a sample allocation calculation row for auditors.

Nora (Finance): Great. Liam  once you confirm the contract language and post the final JE lines I'll attach the memo and close out. If it's agent treatment we'll need a follow-up thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
